name: Hands-on, Hands-off
summary: Each hand can grab objects either directly or, when it is away from the object, indirectly by looking and pinching (Gaze + Pinch), so the two hands can mix direct and gaze-assisted input.
howItWorks: When a hand is within 5 cm of an object it interacts directly; otherwise a pinch acts on the object the user looks at (Gaze + Pinch), with a funnel drawn from the thumb to the object. This gives four bimanual modes: D+D, D+I (non-dominant hand holds the object directly, dominant hand picks and drags parts by gaze), I+D (non-dominant hand orients the object indirectly so it is not occluded while the dominant hand draws on it), and I+I (both indirect). Demonstrated in 3D modelling (voxel colouring, extruding a star mesh, disassembly, drawing on a cube, moving small parts between models). In a study (N=16, Meta Quest Pro) on an orient-then-drag cube task 50 cm away, gaze acquisition was faster but indirect rotation slower (no hand preshaping); I+I needed least movement and was preferred by 9 of 16, followed by D+I.

relationships.note: Applies Gaze + Pinch per hand and switches to direct grasp when a hand reaches the object.
